feedback.product: Tall seat (3/4 in taller through the middle, complete with base, foam and gripper cover)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester 6 ft 0; stock foam broken in (about 15 hours). Two shorter testers (5 ft 9-10) also tried it. Price stated USD 129.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: firmer, flatter seat that removes the sunken pocket feel of worn stock foam; easier sit-to-stand and a more neutral attack position into corners. Suits: riders about 5 ft 9 and up who feel they sit in the bike. Downsides: tester felt 1/2 in would have been enough; would add a ribbed cover for grip. Verdict: worth the money for a roomier rider triangle.

feedback.product: Pro Circuit vs FMF 4.1 titanium muffler systems (comparison)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back on track against the stock system. FMF price stated USD 1099.99; both save about 1.5 lb over stock (FMF figure).
feedback.observed: Changed: Pro Circuit gives more low-end connection and lets you lug third gear; FMF pulls harder through the mid and has a freer top. Both lose over-rev to stock. FMF insert in adds back pressure and bottom end at the cost of some mid freedom. Suits: riders wanting a lighter system with a more linear feel than stock. Downsides: stock system is already very good; Pro Circuit does not keep the stock heat shield. Verdict: both match or beat stock in places; pick PC for bottom, FMF for mid/top.

feedback.product: Power Flow filter kit (aluminium mounting plate, open cage, billet knob, no backfire screen)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Dyno and track. Price stated USD 259.95.
feedback.observed: Changed: better filter sealing and airflow; more rpm response out of corners and pull in loamy berms. Suits: riders wanting a cheap power gain and a better seal than the stock cage. Downsides: with no backfire screen, dirt can drop into the boot during filter changes (vacuum it out before turning the throttle). Verdict: recommended; about one horsepower for far less than a muffler.
feedback.measured: Almost 1 hp gain on the dyno (as stated).

feedback.product: Factory 4.1 RCT stainless full system with carbon end cap
feedback.author: Michael Allen
feedback.conditions: Fitted after stock system turned raspy at about 20 hours; over 10 hours on the FMF at time of writing.
feedback.observed: Changed: with the spark arrestor insert in, slightly more bottom end and a slightly longer mid than stock, over-rev about equal; insert out trades torque for over-rev. Suits: riders wanting trail legality plus a tunable insert. Downsides: gains over stock are small; sticker bubbles from heat; FMF has no repack service, repack yourself about every 20 hours. Verdict: well made, modest but real gains; tester kept insert in.

feedback.product: Pro Circuit Works pipe + R-304 silencer vs FMF pipe and silencer
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Two riders including a 14-year-old coming up from an 85. Needle clip raised to position 2 (from 3), best from sea level to 3500 ft.
feedback.observed: Changed: Pro Circuit adds bottom and mid pull, deeper sound, less clutch work; FMF pulls longer on top and suits fast tracks. Suits: PC for tight tracks and kids moving up from 85s; FMF for GP-style fast tracks. Downsides: PC signs off earlier on top; FMF slower to come on out of corners. Verdict: both better than stock; younger tester preferred PC by a nose.

feedback.product: Billet linkage (pull-rod) arms, 143.5 mm (stock 142.0 mm)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Shock HSC opened 1/4 turn after the first session to soften acceleration chop.
feedback.observed: Changed: rear sits higher, flatter and less front-heavy off throttle; better braking-bump control and easier lean mid to exit of corners; more rear traction once HSC softened. Suits: aggressive riders chasing braking-bump control. Downsides: firmer rear off throttle if you are not pushing; corner entry not improved. Verdict: positive change for fast riders, not a priority buy for relaxed weekend riders.

feedback.product: Three-way full system comparison: FMF, Yoshimura, Akrapovic Evolution
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back with stock. Prices stated: FMF USD 1499.99, Yoshimura USD 1499.99, Akrapovic USD 1549.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: FMF best bottom end and low/mid rpm response; Yoshimura best mid pull and top rpm response; Akrapovic best top end, over-rev and controllability, with less engine braking and much quieter. Akrapovic with quiet inserts let the tester go from map 2 to map 1. Suits: owners who want a broader, more forgiving connection rather than more power. Downsides: Akrapovic stickers discolour and blow off; costly. Verdict: all three beat stock by calming the chassis in different ways.
feedback.measured: Weights: FMF 8.5 lb, Yoshimura 8.4 lb, Akrapovic 8.4 lb. Sound: FMF 121.1 dB, Yoshimura 116.8 dB, Akrapovic 116.1 dB (Keefer figures).

feedback.product: Vortex aftermarket ECU with XPR maps (10 maps, low/mid/high trim knobs)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Mapped to a Pro Circuit exhaust; VP Pro 6 map too strong down low, so a VP T4/pump-fuel map was made. Cost about USD 1000 as stated.
feedback.observed: Changed: broader, smoother bottom with more pull in second and third, crisper mapping with no decel pop. Suits: picky, competitive riders who like stock character but want more control and pull. Downsides: lose Power Tuner features (maintenance log, run time); expensive; benefit smaller than on a KTM because Yamaha stock mapping is good. Verdict: tester happier with it but says most riders can stay on the stock ECU.

feedback.product: Recommended bar bends for 2020 Suzuki RM-Z450/250 and Kawasaki KX450/250
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester preference guide; heights by rider size.
feedback.observed: Changed: Suzuki stock bend has a lot of sweep and feels small; tester prefers Pro Taper EVO SX Race (W800 H87 R54.5 S54) or ODI Podium Flight CountryBoy (W803 H92), Pro Taper EVO Factory Suzuki for 6 ft 0-6 ft 2. Kawasaki: keep 7/8 bars (Renthal 983 W808 H95), Pro Taper Fuzion Henry/Reed as oversize option. Suits: riders wanting a roomier cockpit. Downsides: 7/8 bars flex more for aggressive riders. Verdict: personal-fit guidance, not a single product test.

feedback.product: CNC aluminium throttle tube (Teflon-coated inside)

bike.model: Honda, Yamaha, Suzuki, Kawasaki and KTM models (sold per model)

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested on a Husqvarna; the tube is sold for most Japanese two- and four-strokes.
feedback.observed: Changed: smaller in the hand than other aluminium tubes and smoother than the stock plastic tube, staying smooth after washes; much stronger in crashes. Suits: riders who break tubes or get arm pump from fat grips. Downsides: slightly stiffer feel on landings than plastic. Verdict: recommended for picky cockpit riders.

feedback.product: 22 mm offset triple clamps (stock 21.5 mm) with one-piece 12 mm-post bar mounts
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Fork 5 mm up in the clamps. Prices stated USD 549.99 clamps, USD 104.95 mounts.
feedback.observed: Changed: lower clamp grips 12 mm higher, adding flex; calmer corner entry without off-throttle front wiggle and better stability in chopped ruts; three cone durometers tune bar-mount give. Suits: RM-Z450 riders wanting a more forgiving front without losing turning. Downsides: anodising fades if left in the sun; soft cones can feel vague for fast riders. Verdict: mostly a positive handling change, real value.

feedback.product: 3.0 lowering footpegs (2 mm lower, 10 mm back on 2016+ YZ450F; 57 mm wide)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester 6 ft 0; bar mounts in rear hole. Price stated USD 149.95. Reuses stock pins.
feedback.observed: Changed: feet land on the balls more naturally, hips sit further back, easier standing through ruts; rearward move felt more than the height change. Suits: taller, long-legged Yamaha riders. Downsides: thread-on cleats rather than teeth; tester wanted an even lower option. Verdict: small but useful ergonomic gain.

feedback.product: Rubber-mount mod for an aftermarket muffler using the stock grommet
feedback.author: Matt Sirevaag
feedback.conditions: Test bike broke a muffler bracket with a solid-mounted aftermarket muffler.
feedback.observed: Changed: drilling the aftermarket muffler mount to 5/8 in and fitting the stock rubber grommet and hardware protects the subframe tab. Suits: any KX450 owner fitting a solid-mount aftermarket can. Downsides: slight float at the muffler rear (no vibration noticed). Verdict: cheap, easy fix worth doing.

feedback.product: Ti-6 full muffler system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock muffler sounded blown out even new. Tested by adult and a 14-year-old.
feedback.observed: Changed: a little more bottom-end pull than stock (unusual for PC), stronger mid with no empty feel after shifting to third, top pulls harder, over-rev unchanged. Screen out gives more low rpm response but loses mid; punching a small hole in the screen is a middle option. Suits: riders wanting pull out of deep, tilled corners. Downsides: softer initial low-rpm response than stock. Verdict: pleased; pair with the "Chavez" map for more pull.

feedback.product: Vented air box lid cover
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested on a 2020 YZ250F and a 2021 YZ450F, stock filter cage and also with a Twin Air Power Flow. Price stated USD 80.
feedback.observed: Changed: crisper, lighter feel and more mid rpm in third gear on the YZ250F; little difference on the YZ450F. Suits: YZ250F riders wanting a cheap bit of bottom-end and response. Downsides: louder intake noise; filter gets dirtier in sand and silt; larger-vent versions too loud. Verdict: noticeable but not dramatic, good value on the 250F.

feedback.product: Momentum steel clutch basket (heavier than stock aluminium)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: 2021 YZ450F test bike; paired with a Power Tuner TP 5 map to reduce engine braking. Price stated USD 310. About 90 minutes to fit.
feedback.observed: Changed: acts like added flywheel: calmer delivery out of ruts, less wheelspin on hard pack, chassis more planted with more front traction off throttle. Suits: riders on loamy-to-hard-pack tracks; less needed in soft East Coast dirt. Downsides: slightly more engine braking. Verdict: worth it to smooth the YZ450F.

feedback.product: Linkage system for 2021 KX250 and 2019-2021 KX450
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Light rider 125 lb (stock spring) and Keefer (moved from 54 to 56 N/mm as PC recommends, sag 103 mm). Also tried with PC re-valved suspension. Price stated USD 445.
feedback.observed: Changed: plusher small-bump feel, more end-stroke support and more rear traction; lighter riders can avoid a spring change, heavier riders need about 0.2 kg/mm stiffer. Suits: light riders and aggressive heavier riders who sit low in the stroke. Downsides: expensive; may need a spring change. Verdict: improves comfort and traction.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Quiet inserts left in. Price stated USD 1547; about 1.5 lb lighter than stock.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother roll-on and longer mid pull, more over-rev, less abrupt second-gear hit and less engine braking (fork feels less harsh on decel bumps); very quiet. Tester moved from map 2 to map 1. Suits: riders who find the stock CRF450R too aggressive and tiring. Downsides: less mid-range recovery than stock; expensive. Verdict: one of the best systems on the bike, but a mapped Vortex ECU does more for less money.

feedback.product: RS-12 stainless full system (rubber-mounted to subframe)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back with stock. Price stated USD 850.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother build from about 5000-7000 rpm, less on/off feel, calmer mid-corner, stronger pull out of corners and earlier third-gear shifts, better hard-pack traction, top equal or slightly more over-rev. Rubber mount protects the subframe tab. Suits: riders wanting pull and traction plus a better sound. Downsides: less snappy throttle response than FMF or stock; still looks large. Verdict: a good buy, stainless lasts longer than titanium.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock gearing; Power Tuner map tuned to suit. Price stated USD 1300; 1.5 lb lighter than stock.
feedback.observed: Changed: no extra bottom end, but harder and longer pull mid to top, better over-rev, freer revving with less engine braking that helps corner entry; easier to roll third. Suits: riders wanting mid/top and connection with a clean fit under the side panel. Downsides: cost; no low-end gain. Verdict: excellent once mapped; tester pairs it with an XPR-mapped Vortex ECU for best results.

feedback.product: Showa fork and shock re-valve with spring change
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester had previously used only spring changes and a PC link; with the re-valve the stock linkage was used. Sag 103 mm, a little more HSC.
feedback.observed: Changed: flatter on/off throttle ride, no rear kick on big braking bumps, better initial shock control without squatting out of choppy ruts; traction kept. Suits: heavier or aggressive riders for whom springs alone are a band-aid. Downsides: still slightly soft on G-outs and flat landings; tester may ask for more LSC. Verdict: clear improvement over stock; give the tuner detailed rider info.
feedback.measured: Settings: fork 5.4 kg spring, comp 14 out, reb 10 out, height 3 mm; shock 5.8 kg spring, LSC 11 out, HSC 1-1/4 turns out, reb 9 out.

feedback.product: Slip-on vs full system guide: CRF450R and CRF250R
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester summary of systems tried on 2021 Hondas.
feedback.observed: Changed: CRF450R: a slip-on is the best value; FMF slip-on gives snappier response with smoother mid; Yoshimura tames it but feels lethargic low-mid. CRF250R needs a full system: Yoshimura RS-9 less bottom, more mid/top; FMF 4.1 RCT more bottom and mid, less top, much louder (inserts kill its benefit); Pro Circuit Ti-6 better low response, longer mid, deeper sound. Suits: 450 riders wanting to calm the hit; 250 riders wanting low-mid pull. Verdict: slip-on for the 450, full system for the 250.

feedback.product: Two optional Power Tuner maps incl. "Keefer Connection Map"
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Developed over a couple of weeks on MX tracks and tight rocky terrain. Map values are in images, not text.
feedback.observed: Changed: one map for less hit and more rear traction, one for broader pull with more connection. Suits: YZ450FX riders in technical terrain. Downsides: check the map POSITION setting; values not readable as text here. Verdict: tester favourites.

feedback.product: Seat nuts (OEM replacement, press into rear fender)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 29.95 a pair.
feedback.observed: Changed: replaces soft stock seat nuts that strip; uses OEM bolts. Suits: any KX owner with stripped seat threads. Downsides: some work to press in; pricey for nuts. Verdict: peace of mind against losing the seat.

feedback.product: Edge wheel set (stainless spokes, brand-coloured hubs, bike-specific spacers)

bike.model: Yamaha and other Japanese MX models (Suzuki not offered at time)

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Nearly 50 hours of use. Price stated USD 639. Sizes 21x1.60 front, 19x1.85, 19x2.15 or 18x2.15 rear.
feedback.observed: Changed: tough, not overly rigid hub, rims held up, hub colour did not fade; included spacers ease swapping between bikes. Suits: riders wanting a spare or tougher set without paying USD 1500. Downsides: spokes needed truing a few times after break-in; about 0.5 lb heavier than stock (not felt). Verdict: a good-value set the tester would buy.

feedback.product: Offset titanium footpegs (10 mm back or 7 mm down; 300 g per set)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester 6 ft 0, size 10 boots; Pro Taper SX Race bend. Price about USD 300.
feedback.observed: Changed: 7 mm down eased the cramped seated position and made standing easier with no clearance issue; 10 mm back helped seated cornering but put knees awkwardly when braking and made shift/brake harder to reach. Sharp teeth keep you on the balls of the feet. Suits: tall riders on the YZ-F (combine with a tall seat). Downsides: price; 10 mm back too far for him (5 mm suggested). Verdict: pricey but worth it for Yamaha cockpit comfort.

feedback.product: ROCS Tech triple clamp with PHDS bar mounts
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Hard-pack West Coast tracks.
feedback.observed: Changed: firmer, more stable front when diving into deep ruts with less wallow; PHDS mounts soften slap-down landings. Suits: faster or heavier riders who feel the stock clamp wiggle and dive in deep ruts. Downsides: less compliance leaning into braking bumps, harsher on fast choppy sweepers, worse straight-line comfort, almost 1 lb heavier. Verdict: not worth it on this Yamaha for most riders (worked better on a KTM).

feedback.product: Factory Fatty pipe vs Gnarly pipe, each with Powercore 2 silencer
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: With the Gnarly the needle clip was raised one and the main jet dropped one size.
feedback.observed: Changed: Fatty cleans up the rich bottom, adds mid pull from second to third and longer top/over-rev; Gnarly adds bottom hit, lugability, recovery and rear traction, mid only slightly better than stock. Suits: Fatty for faster tracks and revving; Gnarly for tight tracks and four-stroke style riders. Downsides: Fatty slightly less rear traction; Gnarly runs rich on top and needs rejetting, still less top than Fatty. Verdict: both nice upgrades over stock.
feedback.other_mods: Gnarly test: clip up one, main jet down one size.

feedback.product: High Performance Engine Kit (tested with stock cams; GYTR/FMF muffler, insert out)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Raced in a Keefer vs Keefer event. Tested with stock cams and the FMF system insert out.
feedback.observed: Changed: more mid torque in soft dirt, wider third-gear cornering window, freer revving with less engine braking, slightly more top and over-rev per gear. Suits: vets and amateurs wanting a factory-tested engine package instead of a USD 2500-5000 custom build. Downsides: lacks low rpm response (possibly the muffler insert out); still less over-rev than KTM/Honda for high-revving B riders; rewards short shifting. Verdict: worth the money for riders who want engine work; add GYTR cams or a Vortex map for more top.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Borrowed after a MotoConcepts team test. Price stated USD 1547; about 2 lb lighter than stock.
feedback.observed: Changed: wider pull than the FMF, softer hit, less engine braking, very quiet; tester moved from map 2 to map 1. Durable packing. Suits: deep-pocket owners already buying a system. Downsides: fiddly to line up on install; costly. Verdict: one of the best on the 21-22 CRF450R, but a mapped Vortex ECU is better value; best of all combined.

feedback.product: RS-12 stainless full system
feedback.author: Keefer Inc Testing staff
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back with stock same days. Prices stated: slip-on USD 719, stainless full USD 949, titanium full USD 1259. Under 20 minutes to fit.
feedback.observed: Changed: can hold second longer out of tight inside ruts without slipping the clutch, quicker recovery when a gear high, lighter feel in the mid, big gain mid to top with harder pull per gear. Suits: 2022 CRF250R riders wanting mid-top. Downsides: no extra low-end response; louder (throaty, not obnoxious). Verdict: a true bolt-on benefit, recommended.

feedback.product: Pro Circuit T-6 stainless system, with HGS and FMF compared
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Ti-6 versions hard to get, so stainless T-6 used.
feedback.observed: Changed: PC: bit more bottom pull, strong mid with no empty feel in third, harder top, over-rev unchanged, softer initial response. HGS: PC-like bottom, weaker mid, most top/over-rev (suits sand). FMF: most bottom, mid between PC and HGS, short top. Suits: PC for all-round pull, HGS for sand and revving, FMF for bottom. Downsides: PC screen-out gains response but loses mid and sound. Verdict: pleased with the PC.

feedback.product: Air Flow Kit (two filters, base plate, cage, taller Cycra airbox cover)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: About 30 minutes to fit. Price stated USD 150. Compared with the Twin Air Powerflow kit he had run.
feedback.observed: Changed: quicker low rpm response, freer revving, more mid pull and top/over-rev; claimed one horsepower; filter seals better than stock. Suits: riders wanting more pull in second without buying a muffler. Downsides: louder intake noise; no backfire screen so dirt can fall in on filter changes (lay the bike on its side). Verdict: tester would buy it before an aftermarket muffler; prefers Twin Air aluminium parts but cannot feel a power difference.

feedback.product: Hydraulic folding clutch lever and six-way Power Lever (brake)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Used on a KX250 by Aden with crashes; Power Lever flip chips 14-19 mm; combined with a Braking Batfly rotor. Prices stated: clutch USD 79.99, Power Lever USD 129.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: wider blade than the skinny stock lever (no blisters), more linear engagement, folds and survived crashes; brake feel tunable, all testers chose the 16 mm chip for a firm but not touchy brake. Suits: any KX owner tired of bent levers or the thin stock blades. Downsides: none noted. Verdict: good purchase, lifetime guarantee.

feedback.product: Titanium footpegs (6Al4V, 60x90 mm platform, 11 oz)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock springs reused. Price stated USD 389.95.
feedback.observed: Changed: flat stance like OEM, much more grip on the balls of the feet thanks to sharp teeth, self-clean better than OEM, held up. Suits: riders who slip off dull stock pegs. Downsides: price; no offset options. Verdict: best FLO pegs they have run.

feedback.product: Fork and shock re-valve (average blue-collar rider)
feedback.author: Preston Jordan
feedback.conditions: Returning rider, mostly desert trail riding; sag not checked (editor notes this).
feedback.observed: Changed: far more comfortable and predictable than stock, made small chop manageable. Suits: returning or average riders wanting comfort. Downsides: headshake while standing in whoops remained, possibly setup or chassis rigidity. Verdict: rider calls it the most comfortable suspension he has had.

feedback.product: Titanium front engine mounts (soft and medium) and stainless top mounts (medium)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Two riders, one about 140 lb B class. Prices stated: front mounts USD 219.99, top mounts USD 199.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: medium front mounts gave wider tyre contact feel and more front traction mid-corner but made the front sit low (stinkbug) off throttle; soft front + medium top kept the traction, removed the low-front feel and added chatter and braking-bump compliance. Top mounts alone help slap-down and first-bump comfort. Suits: riders who find the KX250 vague mid-corner. Downsides: slight wallow under heavy load (jump faces, rolling whoops); a touch more LSC suggested. Verdict: soft front / medium top was the favourite, clearly felt against stock.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Fitted during a Racer X garage build; almost 20 hours. Price about USD 1600.
feedback.observed: Changed: softer crack of throttle than stock but more roll-on meat, gets on top of deep soft dirt sooner, more mid pull and later shifts thanks to more over-rev; lighter feel flopping into corners. Packing lasted about twice as long as rivals. Suits: faster riders on flowing longer tracks wanting mid-top. Downsides: lose the stock blip response; least low hit of the three tried (Yoshimura, FMF, Akrapovic); big can looks. Verdict: noticeable even for weekend riders, at a steep price.

feedback.product: Battlecross X31 front tire (with X20 rear)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Front-steering rider; 13.5-14 psi. X31 rear not available at the time.
feedback.observed: Changed: more compliant carcass than X30 yet a stiffer-feeling sidewall for lean in flat corners; predictable break-away, bump comfort close to a Dunlop MX3S; consistent over six hours and wears better than an MX3S. Suits: front-steering riders on soft-to-intermediate dirt that hardens through the day. Downsides: less carcass comfort than a Pirelli MX32 Mid-Soft; MX3S slightly better on soft terrain. Verdict: impressive soft-intermediate front.

feedback.product: Nissin/Brembo hybrid front brake ("Dubach method"): KTM Brembo master cylinder on stock YZ-F caliper and 270 mm carrier
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Parts listed: stock 2022 YZ-F hose (needs 2022 YZ-F caliper carrier), KTM master cylinder 54813001200, spare Brembo lever 54813002100, KTM banjo bolt 50213025000, Yamaha caliper 1C3-2580T-00-00, pads 5MV-W0045-01-00. Move the thin pad clip to the 270 mm carrier.
feedback.observed: Changed: replaces the spongy stock Yamaha front brake feel with a more linear, stronger lever than even an all-Brembo set-up, per the tester. Suits: Yamaha riders unhappy with front brake feel. Downsides: mix of parts from two makers; must match the pad clip. Verdict: best-feeling front brake he had used in a while.

feedback.product: 4.1 slip-on muffler
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Compared with stock before a dual-injector kit was fitted. Best map with it: "Keefer Free Feeling" (on Keefer site). Five-minute install.
feedback.observed: Changed: insert out loses some bottom end; insert in keeps most of the stock bottom, stays quiet and trail-legal; adds mid and a little top; saves over 1 lb. Suits: owners whose stock can turns raspy or who want a bit more mid/top. Downsides: repack about every 10 hours or risk burning the can and rivets. Verdict: happy; keep the insert in.

feedback.product: -15 mm down offset footpeg mounts (1018 steel)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester 6 ft 0; tried in Oklahoma ruts, not East Coast conditions. Price stated USD 240 a set; limited quantity via email.
feedback.observed: Changed: lowers the peg from the mount (cleaner than an offset peg), less bent leg seated, easier to get on the balls of the feet. Suits: riders 6 ft 1 and over (tester preferred -7 mm pegs at 6 ft 0). Downsides: steel is heavy; pegs catch ruts a little easier. Verdict: good value lowering option others cannot match.

feedback.product: 4.1 stainless full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Gearing 13/51 kept; insert left in. Price stated USD 949.99. Repack 10-12 hours.
feedback.observed: Changed: initial crack mellowed but second/third-gear pull out of corners clearly better, more recovery and rear traction, longer mid with better response; top and over-rev about stock; just over 1 lb lighter; much better sound. Suits: riders wanting low-mid pull (PC gives more top). Downsides: stainless looks plainer than titanium (but slip joints last longer). Verdict: a reasonable upgrade over stock.

feedback.product: "Control Torque" (Yamaha R&D) and "Keefer Exciting Connect" maps
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map grids published as images.
feedback.observed: Changed: Control Torque softens roll-on and limits the free-revving feel exiting corners, helpful on rough tracks; Exciting Connect adds low-end excitement and fills the gap before the big mid hit so second-gear roll-on is less abrupt. Suits: riders caught out by the YZ450F mid-range surge. Verdict: optional maps worth trying.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested with stock gearing and Keefer maps. Price about USD 1600.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother roll-on and more rear-wheel connection without breaking loose, harder and longer pull down straights, better over-rev, less engine braking aiding corner entry. Suits: riders who value control and traction over low-end snap. Downsides: no extra low rpm response; expensive. Verdict: excellent and under-rated, you get what you pay for.

feedback.product: WP Pro Components fork and Trax shock fitted to a Kawasaki
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester 175 lb; TCD Racing valving; Glen Helen and softer tracks. About USD 6000 total as stated.
feedback.observed: Changed: Trax shock gave better braking-bump comfort and rear traction in choppy shallow ruts, with a wider adjustment range than the stock Showa (HSC tweak fixed a high rear); fork clickers make clear changes. Suits: vet A-B riders about 175-195 lb chasing comfort. Downsides: very expensive; shock is awkward to fit (bigger reservoir); slight deflection on heavy throttle across bumps. Verdict: tester would choose this over a Showa A-kit for plushness.

feedback.product: Recommended bar bends for 2023 Suzuki RM-Z250/450
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tester fit guide by rider height; stock bar mount height.
feedback.observed: Changed: stock Suzuki bend has much sweep and feels small; preferred Pro Taper EVO SX Race (W800 H87 R54.5 S54); tall riders Renthal Fatbar 827 cut to 803 mm; short riders Pro Taper EVO MX Race cut to 803 mm. FASST Co Flexx bars suggested for bad wrists. Suits: riders wanting a more open cockpit. Verdict: fit guidance, not a product test.

feedback.product: "Keefer Race" and "Keefer Connection Torque" maps, TC set to Low
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map grids published as images; TH% POSITION values changed; traction control must be on LOW.
feedback.observed: Changed: Race map for second motos, Connection Torque for first motos; both usable all day. Suits: a wide range of riders on race day. Downsides: set POSITION and TC correctly or the maps will not match. Verdict: tester race-day maps.

feedback.product: Engine mounts: solid 9 mm titanium front plate (replaces split 4 mm plates)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: About 50 hours on stock and 20 on FCP; tried across three suspension specs on two bikes. Price stated USD 429.
feedback.observed: Changed: less harshness into braking bumps, more front-tyre feel leaning on throttle, calmer unload downhill, better edge traction and straight-line stability, consistent across suspension specs. Suits: 2023 YZ450F riders wanting stability and bump comfort. Downsides: initial lean into corners slightly heavier; coloured finish not to his taste. Verdict: worth it if you want more stability; skip if happy with stock.

feedback.product: 2023 KX250/450 clutch master cylinder kit with lever, fitted to a Honda
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tip from Johnny and Preston Campbell; quick ride. Stock Honda line can be flipped end to end for better routing. Under USD 200 as stated.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother pull and a longer engagement window than the on/off stock Honda clutch. Suits: CRF450R owners who dislike the narrow stock clutch engagement. Downsides: only a short ride reported. Verdict: simple, cheap and much better.

feedback.product: Ti-6 full system (insert and screen left in)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 1270; about 1.5 lb lighter. Paired with the "CHA" map on Keefer site. Repack every 12-15 hours.
feedback.observed: Changed: harder low end, longer second-gear pull and third-gear corners, healthier mid and slightly more top (helps in sand). Insert in smooths the initial hit; insert out is louder and snappier. Suits: KX450 riders wanting more pull and excitement than the linear stock delivery. Downsides: louder than he likes; does not fix the 0-10 % on/off throttle feel. Strong note: reinforce/re-weld the KX subframe muffler tab, it breaks with any aftermarket system even if rubber-mounted. Verdict: happy with the gains.

feedback.product: Power Flow kit (aluminium cage, no backfire screen, support bracket)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: With mapping. Price about USD 250.
feedback.observed: Changed: bracket stops the cage floating and breaking the seal under hard acceleration; more rpm response and pull out of soft loamy berms, snappy yet connected with lots of rear traction. Suits: 2023 YZ450F owners worried about the stock cage seal. Downsides: dirt can drop into the boot on filter changes (lean bike over, vacuum, do not twist throttle). Verdict: best all-round filter system for the YZ450F airbox.

feedback.product: Raptor split triple clamps with interchangeable offset inserts (19-25 mm)
feedback.author: Keefer Inc Testing staff
feedback.conditions: Multiple tracks; 24 mm offset chosen (stock 22 mm). 181 g lighter than OE (Talon figure).
feedback.observed: Changed: 24 mm calmed the twitchy, oversteering Honda into corners, better lean stability and less popping out of ruts; split clamp improved slap-down and bump compliance (helps arm pump). Bar-mount plate resists twisting in tip-overs. Suits: 2020-2023 CRF450R riders who find the bike nervous. Downsides: many mount positions can confuse; bar mount must come off to adjust steering stem tension. Verdict: very positive.

feedback.product: REP linkage (flatter first 70 %, more progressive last 30 %) with REP valving
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested on a CRF450RWE with REP valving; REP runs a spring about four rates lighter with this link.
feedback.observed: Changed: acceleration harshness roughly halved, more plush on square edges, more rear traction and track toughness; rear rides less deep in the stroke. Suits: Honda owners fighting a harsh rear on baked, square-edged tracks. Downsides: not all harshness gone; best results tied to REP valving. Verdict: good enough that he wanted to race it on rough tracks.

feedback.brand: Multiple (REP, GET, Akrapovic, Hinson, Works Connection, Dunlop, Twin Air)
feedback.product: Weekend race set-up: GET ECU (stock tune), Akrapovic Evolution, REP suspension, Hinson 9-plate clutch, WC 26 mm ratio lever, Dunlop MX34/MX14
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway, sandy top soil AM and hard pack PM; rider 172 lb; 10.6 engine hours; gearing 13/49; holeshot 140 mm; tyres 13.5 front / 12.5 rear psi; ETS MX18 fuel.
feedback.observed: Changed: Dunlop MX14 rear excellent off the start and in straight-line drive; GET ECU gives linear roll-on and broader pull; REP fork better small-bump comfort and lean initiation; Akrapovic smooths bottom-to-mid and adds traction out of choppy corners; WC 26 mm lever ratio gives wider, less grabby engagement; Hinson 9-plate pack resists fade. Downsides: stock seat shape painful (thin foam edges); shock wants more comfort on acceleration chop. Verdict: a race-ready template; result DNQ due to a crash, not the parts.
feedback.measured: REP spec fork KK2551BF C12 R11 height 2 mm; shock KK2551BS LSC 10 HSC 1.25 R12, sag 104 mm.
feedback.other_mods: Pro Taper SX Race bar, Renthal full-waffle soft grips, WC perch, WC offset footpeg mounts and Pro Pegs, Renthal sprockets, DID ERT3 chain, WC Pro Launch, Polisport plastics, Blud 10/40 oil.

feedback.product: Lower triple clamp bolt spacer mod (13 mm OD x 5 mm aluminium spacer drilled to M8, 15-18 Nm)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock clamps and 22 mm offset; West Coast hard pack; back-to-back at several tracks; tester used 16 Nm.
feedback.observed: Changed: more front traction on lean and better feel on sharp decel bumps; front more planted when chopping the throttle; can open corners wider without push. Suits: riders who find the 2023 front light in shallow ruts. Downsides: not tried with aftermarket clamps; torque choice changes the effect. Verdict: cheap mod that gives some aftermarket-clamp feel.

feedback.product: Top mods for the 2023 KX250: seat nuts, side panel cut-out, steering bearing grease, 13/51 gearing, linkage
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Several 2023 KX250s ridden by a teenage B rider.
feedback.observed: Changed: cutting the snout off the left side panel opens the airbox intake for more low-end and response (free); steering head bearings arrive with no grease and fail in under 20 hours unless greased; 13/51 closes the 2-3 gap and helps starts; stock KYB fork too stiff for riders under about 165 lb; PC or Ride Engineering linkage with 102 mm sag adds rear traction. Suits: new 2023 KX250 owners. Downsides: some are durability chores rather than performance. Verdict: the 2023 is more reliable than earlier KX250s but grease the steering bearings first.

feedback.product: Full linkage system (pull rods and knuckle) for 2023 KX450 / KX450SR
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Sag moved from 105-106 mm to 103 mm; shock spring raised two rates (5.7 to 6.0 kg). Price stated USD 475 plus spring.
feedback.observed: Changed: drives through square edges under acceleration, more rear traction, and the front tracks better mid-corner. Suits: KX450 riders wanting cornering and traction. Downsides: must go up at least two spring rates or the rear feels mushy; cost. Verdict: a bigger change than most linkages he has tested; everyone will feel it.

feedback.product: "Wide Top" seat foam, stock height
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 99.99. Taller foams available.
feedback.observed: Changed: squarer, box-shaped top stops bottoming on the seat pan when loaded and cured the soreness from the stock seat. Suits: 2023-24 YZ450F riders who get sore. Downsides: still take the seat off before washing. Verdict: a must-have for comfort.

feedback.product: Hydraulic clutch kit (Brembo-based) for 2023-2024 YZ450F
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back with cable for starts; rider covers the clutch constantly; 10/40 non-synthetic oil. Price stated USD 299.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: engagement moves toward the end of the lever throw with a wider, less on/off window; more consistent starts; lighter pull with enough feel at the engagement point. Suits: riders who prefer hydraulic feel or keep re-adjusting a cable. Downsides: plate life unchanged (about 10-12 hours for this hard user). Verdict: tester kept it; stay with cable if it works for you.

feedback.product: Ti-6 full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map used shown on Keefer site. Price stated USD 1400; 1.8 lb lighter. Open-end wrench needed for the headpipe nuts.
feedback.observed: Changed: livelier throttle and lighter side-to-side feel, much harder pull and better pick-up from soft berms, slightly more mid in second and third and more lugability; top/over-rev about stock. Quieter than older Ti-6 with insert in. Suits: 2024 KX450 riders who find the stock bike lethargic down low; vets. Downsides: awkward install. Verdict: a no-brainer for more low-mid.

feedback.product: Ti-6 Pro titanium system (carbon end cap)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Run with the "Keefer Race Map"; dry choppy SoCal tracks. Price stated USD 1352.95; almost 2 lb lighter. Loosely fit the mid pipe before tightening the headpipe nuts.
feedback.observed: Changed: slightly softer response at about 10 % throttle, then stronger mid with crisp mid-rpm response, second and third usable longer, top as stock with slightly more over-rev; more bottom than the Akrapovic. Deeper, quieter note than older Ti-6. Suits: older riders and those wanting connection rather than snap. Downsides: softer low rpm hit (fix with a more aggressive map). Verdict: impressed; spreads power well.

feedback.product: Vented air box lid cover
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock cage and screen, also tried with Twin Air Power Flow. Price stated USD 100.
feedback.observed: Changed: a bit more snap off the bottom and in third-gear mid on the 2024 YZ250F (which lost low end with its new air boot); crisper over square edges. Suits: 2024 YZ250F owners wanting cheap low-end response. Downsides: a lot louder (ear plugs suggested); filter gets dirtier in sand/silt; small effect on the YZ450F. Verdict: noticeable, not dramatic, good value.

feedback.product: 4.1 slip-on muffler
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 899.99; almost 1.5 lb lighter.
feedback.observed: Changed: more usable low-end pull and torque out of corners while staying linear, much better throttle-to-rear-wheel connection on hard pack, livelier over bumps, more mid so third gear corners are more usable; slight top gain. Suits: riders wanting the 2024 KX450 to feel less flat. Downsides: none significant noted. Verdict: you can feel where the money went.

feedback.product: Race 2.0 complete seat (OEM shape, firmer foam)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: About 25 engine hours, washed with seat on (worst case). Price stated USD 349.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: plush but supportive foam that did not break down after 25 hours (stock goes in 8-12); no soreness on multi-day riding; perfect fit. Suits: YZ450F riders whose stock foam collapses; anyone wanting a spare seat. Downsides: cover loses some grip over time; about USD 170 more than foam plus cover. Verdict: pleased; this model needs better foam.

feedback.product: Power Flow kit (uses Power Flow filter)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: About one hour to install (plastics, tank, battery, ECU and subframe off). Price stated USD 214.
feedback.observed: Changed: tabbed filter/cage ensures a proper seal (stock filter can be sucked concave and lets dirt in); small low-mid rpm response gain. Suits: KX450 owners wanting insurance against dirt ingestion. Downsides: painful install; must use the proprietary filter 151129FRX. Verdict: mainly engine protection, not a power mod on this bike.

feedback.product: Race Cups (20-degree offset steering head races)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Sag moved 105 to 103 mm; fork compression may need softening a couple of clicks. Price stated USD 589-599; works with any clamp; also for Kawasaki and Honda.
feedback.observed: Changed: slower but more stable steering, more front-tyre weight and contact on lean, less headshake moving from on to off throttle on rough straights. Suits: riders wanting a calmer YZ450F on fast rough tracks and long bumpy ruts. Downsides: turns a little slower; costly. Verdict: a bigger handling change than some offset clamps; you will feel it.

feedback.product: Evolution titanium full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Stock gearing. Price about USD 1700. Almost 30 hours without repacking.
feedback.observed: Changed: more low-end torque than stock, harder and longer pull mid-top, better over-rev, more rear connection without breaking loose, less engine braking and pitching into corners; very quiet for the power. Suits: riders wanting a quiet, long-lasting system with real gains. Downsides: price. Verdict: excellent, you actually get what you pay for.

feedback.product: RS-12 stainless full system
feedback.author: Eddie Laret and Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: 230 lb rider. Price stated USD 979; system weighs 8 lb 3 oz, almost 2 lb heavier than stock.
feedback.observed: Changed: more low-end torque and mid-rpm response while keeping a smooth, linear delivery; exits corners harder so the bike rides over acceleration chop; small mid-top gain; deeper, slightly quieter note. Suits: heavier riders who find the stock KX450 too lazy. Downsides: heavier than stock; big can. Verdict: a great buy; Yoshimura offers a repack service.

feedback.product: MAKO 360 handlebar mounts (polymer-isolated)
feedback.author: Victor Guerrero and Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen. Price stated USD 439.99-529.99. Weights: stock 15.4 oz, MAKO 29.3 oz. Adds 6 mm bar rise on this bike.
feedback.observed: Changed: little vibration reduction (slight at idle and high rpm) but more forgiveness on bumps and slap-down landings, less hand/arm fatigue. Suits: long-distance trail and desert riders. Downsides: almost double the weight of stock; cannot tie down by the bars; bar pad needs shaping; very expensive. Verdict: real comfort gain but a big spend.

feedback.product: Optional 2025 KX450 map for pull and recovery
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map grid published as an image.
feedback.observed: Changed: more pick-up out of corners and more torque feel in second and third. Important: Kawasaki raised the ignition timing adjustment limit from +1 to +10 for 2025, so this map only works on a 2025; loading it on a 2024 clips timing to +1. Verdict: worth trying on 2025 bikes only.

feedback.product: Swingarm length (pivot to axle) targets by gearing: 13/49, 13/50, 14/52
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Starting measurements from REP Suspension; ballpark values, chain tension affects them.
feedback.observed: Changed: 13/49 with 114 links, 585.4-586.8 mm, sag 105, fork 3 mm = best all-round; 13/48 is more stable but hurts third-gear recovery. 13/50 with 114 links, 581.1-582.6 mm, fork flush, sag 106 = better corner entry for vets. 14/52 with 116 links, 584.7-586.0 mm, fork 2 mm, sag 105 = smoother roll-on and more hard-pack traction. Suits: tinkerers fine-tuning geometry. Verdict: practical gearing and length targets.

feedback.product: Brembo master + Nissin caliper front brake mod (re-visit): 2007 YZ450F-type Nissin caliper and 2007 450 SX-F-type Brembo master for piston sizing
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Same parts list as the 2022 article: current YZ-F hose and caliper carrier, move the pad clip from the 250 mm to the 270 mm carrier.
feedback.observed: Changed: more linear, firmer front brake than the spongy stock Yamaha feel. Suits: current YZ-F riders wanting a stronger lever. Downsides: mixed-brand parts and older-spec pieces to source. Verdict: still his best-feeling front brake set-up.

feedback.product: Ti-6 full system for the 2025 KX250 (new headpipe and muffler)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen, a desert track and Sunfair 42 MX. Price stated USD 1269.95; just over 1.8 lb lighter.
feedback.observed: Changed: a little more bottom pull and snappier response, strong mid with no empty feel in third, pulls harder into the top; over-rev unchanged; much better sound. Cutting the screen out but keeping the insert adds low response; fully insert-out gave the younger rider more mid. Suits: 2025 KX250 riders who find the bike heavy-feeling. Downsides: still wants more low end overall. Verdict: makes the 2025 feel lighter, a positive.

feedback.product: 80 g flywheel weight (welded to your stock flywheel, mail-in service)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tried with several Power Tuner maps. No price given. YZ450FX/WR flywheels do not work with the YZ harness (per Yamaha).
feedback.observed: Changed: calmer rpm build, more rear traction and less front lift on corner exits, more lugability in a high gear without stalling, and no added engine braking. Suits: vets and pros who find the YZ450F a handful on rough or technical tracks. Downsides: none found by tester; must send away your flywheel. Verdict: close to a must-do mod for traction and control.

feedback.product: "Works" silicone Y radiator hose kit with billet water jackets and clamps
feedback.author: Eddie Laret
feedback.conditions: Fitted on the Keefer 2025 KX450 garage build. Price stated USD 399.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: replaces the 2024-25 KX450 temp-sensor jacket and metal water-pump tube with two Y hoses, fewer clamps and joints that could fail. Suits: owners wanting a cleaner, factory look and fewer failure points. Downsides: costly; coolant smell for the first rides (no leak found); do not over-tighten clamps. Verdict: mainly looks, with a small reliability gain.

feedback.product: REP linkage for 2023-2025 YZ450F ("in between" ratio)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Sag 104-105 mm. Stock spring works on 2023-24; 2025 (stock 5.6 N/mm with stiffer stock link) may need one rate up. Price stated USD 450; order by phone/email.
feedback.observed: Changed: on 2023-24 the rear stays up under acceleration (less squat) with more traction and less harshness; on 2025 it adds compliance over chop and stops the rear overpowering the fork off throttle. Works even with stock suspension. Suits: YZ450F riders wanting rear traction and comfort. Downsides: check sag after fitting; not sold online at the time. Verdict: a good buy.

feedback.product: 2025 CRF450R Works Edition baseline settings
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Works Edition (18 mm shock shaft). Heavier spring option for riders over 180 lb.
feedback.observed: Changed: WE fork moves quicker and feels softer mid-stroke than the standard R; shock feels tougher on throttle (vs the R with its emptier end stroke). Suits: CRF450RWE owners needing a start point.
feedback.measured: Fork stock 5.0 N/mm: height flush-2 mm, comp 8-9 out, reb 8 out. Heavier option 5.1 (one 5.2 spring one side): comp 11, reb 9. Shock 56 N/mm, sag 106 mm, LSC 9 out, HSC 1.75 out, reb 10 out.

feedback.product: Fully assembled OEM wheel sets (hub, bearings, seals, rim, spokes, disc, sprocket, rim lock)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Prices stated for YZ450F: front USD 599.99, rear USD 439.99. Blue or black.
feedback.observed: Changed: a ready-to-run spare set including disc and sprocket, which other OEMs do not include. Tester ranks OEM wheel toughness Yamaha, Honda, Kawasaki, Triumph, Suzuki, then KTM group. Suits: Yamaha owners wanting tough spares without aftermarket rigidity worries. Downsides: still need rim tape, tube and tyre. Verdict: great buy.

feedback.product: 23.5 mm offset split triple clamps (redesigned)
feedback.author: Jesse Heninger (owner) via Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Owner test over several weeks at Glen Helen, Cal City and DT1; dry edgy SoCal tracks. Fork raised (Keefer suggests 2 mm stock, up to 5 mm with these).
feedback.observed: Changed: more comfort and flex loading into corners and on slap-downs, calmer chassis in rough sections, less edge-of-tyre deflection. Suits: faster intermediate to pro riders who want stability. Downsides: front less planted exiting flat corners until the fork was raised; novices may not feel much. Verdict: owner gained stability and confidence.

feedback.product: Engine mounts for 2025 KX250
feedback.author: Kris Keefer and Aden Keefer
feedback.conditions: Amateur racer and Keefer; West and East Coast tracks; fork height flush on hard pack, 2 mm in deep East Coast ruts. Price stated USD 450.
feedback.observed: Changed: more front lean-angle grip in flat corners, more planted and less twitchy off throttle, better slap-down and bump touch on soft tall tracks; on-throttle "busy" front not improved but not worse. Suits: KX250 riders wanting comfort and front traction. Downsides: may need fork height and clicker changes; cost. Verdict: noticeable change, worth it if you need front grip.

feedback.product: Aluminium offset footpeg mounts (a further -5 mm down and -5 mm back; 7075-T6)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Over 35 hours. Price stated USD 199.95 a pair (kit includes titanium pins). Works with stock or aftermarket pegs; shifter and brake pedal did not need moving.
feedback.observed: Changed: more cockpit room, less bent knees, easier sit-to-stand, better leverage on the pegs in flat corners, less leg fatigue. Suits: Yamaha riders about 5 ft 10 and taller. Downsides: modest change, not Honda-like ergonomics. Verdict: worthwhile comfort mod.

feedback.product: "Travis Preston" map and "Keefer Exciting Connect" map for 2026 YZ450F
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map grids published as images (Preston map shown blank).
feedback.observed: Changed: Preston map adds low-end excitement because the 2026 is more plugged up than the 2025; Keefer map adds rear connection and torque feel shifting from second to third. Verdict: optional maps to try.

feedback.product: RS-12 stainless full system
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Back-to-back with stock. Prices stated: stainless USD 1149, titanium USD 1679. Under 20 minutes to fit.
feedback.observed: Changed: holds second longer out of tight ruts without slipping the clutch, quicker recovery, lighter mid, clear mid-to-top gain and crisper third-gear response; keeps the 2025-26 low end. Suits: CRF250R riders wanting mid-top and recovery. Downsides: not much extra low-end response; price. Verdict: a true bolt-on benefit.

feedback.product: Pulse replacement front rotor 270 mm (non-floating) with billet hanger for 260-to-270 conversions
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Tested on Honda, Kawasaki and Yamaha. Prices stated: Yamaha/Kawasaki replacement USD 120; 260-to-270 kits USD 179.95 (OEM Yamaha rotor USD 155).
feedback.observed: Changed: slightly stronger initial bite on the Honda with no drag; no change on the YZ450F versus the stock floating rotor. Suits: Yamaha/Kawasaki owners needing a cheaper replacement, or Honda owners wanting an oversize rotor. Downsides: gains are small. Verdict: good-value replacement, modest upgrade.

feedback.product: RS-12 full titanium system (hydroformed muffler)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Fitted to the Keefer 2026 CRF450R garage build with no other engine work. Price stated USD 1700; about 1.8 lb lighter.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother low-rpm delivery and more rear connection, calmer mid-to-exit cornering, earlier throttle, smoother but torquier third-gear pull; top/over-rev about stock; quieter, nicer sound; packing outlasts rivals. Suits: CRF450R riders wanting traction and cornering. Downsides: steep price; large-looking can. Verdict: makes the Honda corner and perform better.

feedback.product: 2026 YZ450F map to reduce engine braking
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Map grid published as an image.
feedback.observed: Changed: relaxes the 2026 engine on decel so the extra engine braking (versus 2024-25) no longer upsets the chassis into corners; easier to roll corners. Suits: 2026 owners who notice the added engine braking. Verdict: try it if you feel it.

feedback.product: Ti-6 Pro "BC" full system (no carbon end cap)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Insert in for AMA events; insert out gives more low snap. Map used shown on site. Price stated USD 1400.
feedback.observed: Changed: livelier throttle, lighter-feeling bike, harder pull and pick-up from soft berms, more lugability and slightly more mid in second-third, second gear longer so third comes sooner; top slightly better. Quieter than older Pro. Suits: 2024-26 KX450 riders wanting low-mid; vets. Downsides: those wanting a carbon cap. Verdict: a no-brainer where the price is felt on track.

feedback.product: Small Diameter Clutch Kit (five coil springs, Billetproof hard parts)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Deep sand tracks and Glen Helen to provoke fade. Price stated USD 1224.99. Previously ran the Hinson Billetproof complete clutch.
feedback.observed: Changed: positive lever feel with more pressure, clear bite point, more pop off corners (more low rpm feel) and no engagement drift or fade under abuse; stock clutch fades, drifts and slips after several hours. Suits: KX450 riders in deep dirt or long motos. Downsides: expensive. Verdict: a must-have for hard use.

feedback.product: APEX manual clutch system (Fixed-Pin hub, TorqDrive pack, billet pressure plate and cover)
feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: Several hours. Price stated USD 1199.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother, more consistent engagement under abuse, steel-on-steel hub avoids notching, more friction plates improve drive and resist fade in sand and long motos. Suits: aggressive riders and racers keeping the bike long term. Downsides: price; spring combinations need setting up. Verdict: one of the best manual clutch upgrades for the KX450.

feedback.product: Mod Squad 2020 CRF450R: Rekluse TorqDrive clutch pack, FMF Factory 4.1 RCT Ti dual system, enzo fork/shock revalve and spring tubes, ODI RC4 Flite bars
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Built after their 2020 450 shootout (CRF was third). Prices stated: enzo fork and shock revalve USD 200 each, spring tubes USD 250, HS shock adjuster USD 250, FMF USD 1499.99, Rekluse TorqDrive pack USD 349, ODI bar USD 99.95.
feedback.observed: Changed: TorqDrive pack (12 fibres / 11 steels in the stock space) cured the stiff stock clutch pull and greatly improved low-end drive so taller gears became easy; FMF gives a throaty note. Bars flatter and straighter than the stock sweep. Suits: CRF450R owners with a heavy clutch pull. Downsides: you may need to re-learn acceleration points. Verdict: they call the TorqDrive the best dollar-for-dollar performance part.

feedback.product: Core Manual TorqDrive clutch (hub, pressure plate, TorqDrive pack)
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Paired with a Yoshimura RS-12 exhaust. Price stated USD 999 (TorqDrive pack alone USD 359 with stock basket/hub).
feedback.observed: Changed: brought back the off-idle snap the RS-12 exhaust had taken away (Power Tuner could not fully restore it), less clutch slip so more traction and forward drive, quick fan of the lever recovers mid-corner mistakes. Separately, the RS-12 gave stronger mid and much better top but average testers missed the low-end response. Suits: riders who lost bottom end with an exhaust. Downsides: may have to rethink throttle into jumps. Verdict: rated the best performance value.

feedback.product: Air Flow Kit (two filters, new cage, larger airbox cover)
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 149.99. 5-10 minute install.
feedback.observed: Changed: noticeable gains in throttle response and top-end power; cleaner-sounding rev; bigger cover gives knee grip. Suits: YZ250F/YZ450F owners wanting more top before engine or ECU work. Downsides: stock-size filters no longer fit; needs a new airbox graphic. Verdict: try this before more involved mods.

feedback.brand: enzo racing / Technical Touch Moto-Master / Hinson / FMF / Maxxis
feedback.product: Mod Squad 2024 CRF450R upgrades: enzo revalve, Moto-Master 270 mm front rotor kit and rear caliper, Hinson plates and cover, FMF Factory 4.1 RCT, Maxxis SI tyres
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Goal: comfort and predictability. Prices stated: enzo fork revalve USD 220 plus parts; Moto-Master oversize front kit USD 308, rear caliper USD 136, pads USD 39.95; Hinson plates USD 219.99, cover USD 199.99; FMF Ti USD 1374.99 (stainless USD 1049.99, same performance); Maxxis SI front USD 102, rear USD 139.
feedback.observed: Changed: FMF 4.1 evens out the powerband for easier control over a moto without losing power; Moto-Master brakes rated the best they have used; Maxxis SI a big step over the ST in grip and life. Suits: CRF450R owners who find it rigid and unpredictable. Downsides: no per-part back-to-back data given. Verdict: an easier, more trustworthy bike.

feedback.product: Hydraulic clutch kit (Magura master, braided line, slave)
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Fitted at the track in under 20 minutes for back-to-back laps; compared with a Works Connection Pro Perch cable set-up. Lever reach set at notch 10 of 22. Price stated USD 299.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: smoother, less grabby engagement makes slipping into the powerband more controllable and less likely to break the rear loose on hard pack; better starts for them. Suits: most riders on the hard-hitting YZ450F. Downsides: cable gives a more precise feel taking up chain slack on the line; lever felt firm versus the WC perch. Verdict: staying on the bike all year.

feedback.product: Factory 4.1 RCT titanium system with carbon end cap
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: All three maps tried, spark arrestor in and out. Price stated USD 1374.99 (stainless/aluminium version USD 1049.99 with the same performance).
feedback.observed: Changed: broader, more controllable hit with slightly better off-idle response, linear pull into high rpm; Map 1 felt excellent and let the shock work in acceleration chop; Map 3 became manageable. Spark arrestor out = louder and less low-end roll-on. Suits: 2025 CRF450R riders wanting better, not more, power. Downsides: price; Map 2 still feels slow. Verdict: leave the arrestor in; easier to ride.

feedback.product: T-6 stainless system
feedback.author: Mike Bush (Swapmoto Live)
feedback.conditions: Perris Raceway; mostly a video review, short written summary.
feedback.observed: Changed: improved power right off idle on a bike whose low-end response and torque are lacking; easy install, throaty note. Suits: 2026 KX250 riders wanting low-end. Verdict: tester impressed.

feedback.product: RS-12 Hybrid full system (header resonance chamber, keeps stock heat shield)
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 1129. Tests at 110 dB; insert makes it 109 dB compliant. Stock 2026 pipe is hard to remove.
feedback.observed: Changed: freer-revving and lighter feel, snappier throttle, and gains low, mid and top over-rev while keeping the 2026 friendly character with no spikes; consistent across maps, so they rode the standard map more. Suits: 2026 owners who find the quieter stock bike a little muted. Downsides: stock system removal is a chore. Verdict: works amazingly well; staying on.

feedback.product: Titanium front and aluminium top engine mount kit
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Magazine staff
feedback.conditions: Kit for 2019-20 KX450. Price stated USD 399 per set.
feedback.observed: Changed: more front traction and bite so inside lines were easier, plusher overall with less fatigue. Suits: riders wanting a plusher, better-turning KX450. Downsides: costly; buy it to fix a specific problem. Verdict: a considerable difference even on a good bike.

feedback.product: T-6 stainless dual exhaust (aluminium canisters, USFS spark arrestors)
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Magazine staff
feedback.conditions: Long-term use. Price stated USD 939.76. Model years not stated in the text (published 2020).
feedback.observed: Changed: power gains across the whole curve with no dips, throatier note; meets AMA amateur sound rules and is trail legal with arrestors. Suits: riders who mix MX and off-road. Downsides: no weight saving over stock; do not pull the arrestor while hot; replace the copper crush washer at the head. Verdict: a cost-effective dual system with real gains.

feedback.product: 2-gallon fuel tank (uses R shrouds on the RX)
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Magazine staff
feedback.conditions: Sold in the US by Checkpoint Off-Road; listed for 2021-22 CRF450R/RX and 2022 CRF250R/RX. Price stated USD 399. Stock R tank 1.6 gal, RX 2.25 gal.
feedback.observed: Changed: on the RX, a much slimmer, less bulky tank with over 40 miles range; on the R, more fuel with no more intrusion than stock. Suits: RX owners who hate the bulky stock tank; R owners going off-road. Downsides: less range than the RX tank; R owners need extra parts. Verdict: they love it on their CRF450RX.

feedback.product: Elite wheelset (17/14 in, billet 6082-T6 hubs, Excel Takasago rims, double drive-side bearing)
feedback.author: Dirt Bike Magazine staff
feedback.conditions: A full year of off-road, high-level off-road racing and amateur national MX. Price about USD 900. Listed for 1998-2023 KX85 standard.
feedback.observed: Changed: survived a year of abuse with only scratches; double bearing adds strength for fast mini riders; reuses OEM spacers; many colour options. Suits: fast or heavy-use KX85 riders. Downsides: expensive; spokes loosened early (watch those next to the rim lock); hub colour can vary. Verdict: well worth it for quality.

feedback.product: Mod Squad 2025 KX450: FMF Factory 4.1 stainless Megabomb, STR fork/shock revalve, STR airbox mods, STR remap of the stock ECU
feedback.author: Swapmoto Live staff
feedback.conditions: Prices stated: FMF USD 1049.99; STR shock revalve from USD 235.95, fork from USD 245.95 plus parts; airbox mods USD 160; stock ECU remap USD 60.
feedback.observed: Changed: exhaust, airbox mods, a remap and firmer suspension took the mild stock KX450 to a bike the testers were happy with. Suits: riders who find the 2025 KX450 too mild. Downsides: no per-part detail in the text. Verdict: little is needed to wake the bike up.

feedback.product: DirtStar ST-X rims laced to Nacstar USA hubs (complete wheelset)
feedback.author: Josh Mosiman (MXA)
feedback.conditions: Raced at three AMA 450 Nationals and Mammoth. Prices stated: ST-X rim front USD 260.85, rear USD 241.72; complete Nacstar/D.I.D wheelset USD 999.
feedback.observed: Changed: stronger than stock with little break-in; only a few spokes needed about 1/8 turn, and about five rear spokes loosened after jumping a huge Hangtown double. ST-X has a stiffer contour than standard DirtStar (softer, better for off-road). Suits: hard-hitting racers wanting a factory look. Downsides: expensive. Verdict: stout wheels, no complaints.

feedback.product: Pro-4 32 mm carburetor with metering rod, Domino throttle and cable
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Multiple mini riders, GP races, high-desert trails and hill climbs; Lectron cold-start procedure followed; only the Torque Jet idle adjusted. Price stated USD 899.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: ended the CRF150R bog, hesitation and constant jetting; strong in every condition and elevation; external adjusters replace jet swaps. Suits: any CRF150R family fighting the stock carb. Downsides: needs active throttle until warm; price. Verdict: no complaints; the carb Honda should have fitted.

feedback.product: Factory Edition SX Slide-N-Guide kit and chain guide
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Listed fit: 2021-2025 CRF450R/RX/WE and 2022-2025 CRF250R/RX. Price stated USD 155.95. Set 65-70 mm chain slack; bolts have little thread in the swingarm.
feedback.observed: Changed: durable chain slider and guide with damping pads that cut chain-slap noise while keeping correct slack. Suits: racers who wear out stock sliders. Downsides: not the cheapest; do not over-torque the swingarm bolts. Verdict: among the best guides available.

feedback.product: Twin Air PowerFlow kit (grommet filter, aluminium cage, L-bracket) plus SRP High Flow airbox cover
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Prices stated: PowerFlow kit USD 249.95, filter USD 36.95, SRP cover USD 100. Stock 2023-24 filter can let dirt in at the front because its rubber strap is too loose.
feedback.observed: Changed: grommeted filter stops dirt getting under the cage; combo revs quicker and broadened the power rather than making it wild; over 2 hp gain claimed for the combo. Suits: pro-level riders wanting more power; most riders just need the grommet filter. Downsides: very loud with the vented cover; no backfire screen on a downdraft intake; about USD 350. Verdict: a win for pros.
feedback.measured: Over 2 hp gain for the combination (as stated).

feedback.product: Rising-rate linkage (revised bell crank) for 2023-2024 CRF250R
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 600; stiffer overall curve lets the shock run a much lighter spring.
feedback.observed: Changed: calmer, more stable rear, more compliant tracking in rough, better square-edge absorption; flatter first three-quarters and more progressive last quarter keep it from riding deep. Suits: CRF250R riders wanting rear comfort. Downsides: needs a spring change, so the total cost rises. Verdict: more initial comfort and a more positive feel in the rough.

feedback.product: Hydraulic clutch kit (Brembo lever, master, braided line, slave seal kit, push rod)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Race-tested. Fits 2023-2025 YZ450F and 2024-2025 YZ450FX (cases designed to accept it). Price stated USD 299.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: broader, more forgiving engagement, no lever play to keep adjusting, calms the YZ450F initial hit and builds confidence. Suits: most riders, especially those used to KTM hydraulics. Downsides: slips badly if you rev against a held clutch before the gate drops, causing wheelies off the line. Verdict: they loved it and will not go back to cable.

feedback.product: PowerFlow kit (base plate, glass-fibre cage, domed pre-oiled filter)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Dyno and track. Subframe must come off to fit. Price stated USD 214.95; vented airbox plug USD 62.95.
feedback.observed: Changed: little felt alone, but it stops dirt getting past the poorly sealing stock flat filter; paired with an FMF or Pro Circuit slip-on the bike came alive. Pro Circuit race mod (trim plastic around the filter plus T-6 slip-on) filled the stock mid dip. Suits: every 2024 KX450 owner as engine insurance. Downsides: long install. Verdict: a longevity mod, not a power mod.
feedback.measured: Dyno: 57.3 to 57.9 hp, torque 35.6 to 35.8 lb-ft with the kit; PC race mod with T-6 slip-on peak torque 37.7 lb-ft.

feedback.product: 2025 RM-Z250 set-up advice: fuel couplers, fork and shock springs
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Ask the MXperts reply to a new owner; 2025 is identical to 2019.
feedback.observed: Changed: use the white coupler (most aggressive, revs faster), skip grey and black; power is best below 8000 rpm so do not over-rev. Forks very stiff: drop 5.0 to 4.8 N/mm (or lower for light riders) and open compression 3-5 clicks from 11 out; shock spring 52 to 50 N/mm with 107 mm sag. Suits: novices; the bike is down almost 6 hp on its class. Verdict: easy to ride once softened.
feedback.measured: Fork 4.8 N/mm, comp 14-16 out; shock 50 N/mm, sag 107 mm.

feedback.product: Gen3 Pro triple clamps with adjustable offset 21-24 mm and stiffening bracket; rubber bar mounts
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen National track. Prices stated: clamps USD 999.95, rubber mounts USD 189.95, solid USD 109.95 (standard Gen3 USD 699.95). Fits 2023-2024 YZ250F/YZ450F.
feedback.observed: Changed: even at stock 22 mm, more front traction and planted cornering without over-tightening the steering stem as a damper; 23 mm best (calmer corner entry, less wiggle, headshake and wag); 24 mm more stable but less nimble. Stiffening bracket too stiff outdoors. Suits: high-level YZ riders. Downsides: price. Verdict: solved their biggest YZ450F handling complaints.

feedback.product: Kawasaki Pro-Pack bolt kit (incl. collared T-nuts, steel fork-guard bolts, M22 axle nut)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 79.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: replaces lost or weak hardware; T-nuts with a 1 mm collar stay in the rear fender; 8 mm hex steel fork-guard bolts replace soft aluminium Allen bolts. Suits: anyone maintaining a KX. Verdict: practical spares kit.

feedback.product: Factory 4.1 RCT titanium slip-on
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Listed for 2019-2025 YZ250F. About six hours on it. Price stated USD 849.99; stock muffler 3 lb heavier. Transfer the stock rubber bushing and collar.
feedback.observed: Changed: same initial crack as stock but more mid-to-top pull to the limiter so gears can be held longer instead of falling flat; far better sound than the loud stock can; packing fine after tip-overs. Suits: YZ250F riders who rev it out on fast tracks. Downsides: not cheap. Verdict: turned the stock bike into a race bike.

feedback.product: Skid plate with Rubber Isolator Mounting System (6061-T6)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Product spotlight (no riding results). Also fits 2024 KX450X. Price stated USD 94.95.
feedback.observed: Changed: protects frame rails and cases without stiffening the frame (rubber-isolated mounts); oil drain hole pre-cut. Suits: KX450/KX450X riders wanting protection. Verdict: spotlight only, no test verdict.

feedback.product: Works Y radiator hose kit with billet fittings and silicone-rated clamps
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: 15-minute install; also for KX450X. Price stated USD 399.99.
feedback.observed: Changed: removes the stock cross-over metal tube and fragile Y-fittings (as factory Kawasaki runs), fewer failure points, high temperature/pressure rating. Suits: racers wanting reliability and colour. Downsides: price; bleed air and check for leaks after. Verdict: positive, matching Keefer findings on the same kit.

feedback.product: Kawasaki rear-fender Perma-Nut (replaces loose T-nut plate)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 14.99 for two.
feedback.observed: Changed: stops the seat/airbox T-nut plate falling out of the fender every time the airbox cover is removed (glue fixes failed). Suits: 2019-2023 KX owners. Verdict: a true fix for a long-standing annoyance.

feedback.product: Rubber-isolated head stays and engine mounts (soft/medium/hard elastomers)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Price stated USD 379.95. Front mounts later strengthened by Luxon. Only made for the YZ450F so far.
feedback.observed: Changed: rubber head stays took the edge off bumps, improved hand feel and made the suspension feel plusher; testers felt the change from stock but not between damper hardnesses. Suits: outdoor riders wanting more comfort. Downsides: not recommended for supercross. Verdict: made an already comfortable chassis more compliant.

feedback.product: Right side-case gasket oil leak
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Two MXA 2025 test bikes leaked within about 3-4 hours; a racer reported replacing the gasket three times.
feedback.observed: Changed: n/a. Observed: oil seeping from the gasket on the right side case under the cylinder, first after a crash and then on a second bike without one. Suits: owners chasing an unexplained right-side leak. Verdict: check and replace the right side-case gasket.

feedback.product: YZ250 and YZ250X carburettor needles (N3EW vs NYHW)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Ask the MXperts technical reply.
feedback.observed: Changed: the YZ250 still uses the N3EW needle (stock since 2007); the 2023 YZ250X uses NYHW, one clip leaner, because its head drops compression from 8.9:1 to 7.9:1 (21.5 to 23.6 cc) with less mid-high ignition advance. Do not lean a YZ250 to NYHW spec; any pipe, porting or head change could make it run lean. Verdict: keep stock YZ250 jetting unless the engine is modified.

feedback.product: Split fork spring trick: one 0.52 and one 0.50 kg/mm spring for an effective 0.51
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Ask the MXperts reply; Showa offers no 0.51 spring.
feedback.observed: Changed: mixing springs gives a 0.51 kg/mm average for owners who find 0.50 soft but 0.52 too stiff; put the stiffer spring in the brake-side leg. 2025 KX450 forks are close to race-ready for vets and novices. Verdict: cheap, simple fix.

feedback.product: PowerFlow kit for 2025-2026 KX250 (hand-screw bolt filter mount)
feedback.author: MXA staff
feedback.conditions: Subframe off to install. Price stated USD 359.95. Only works with the 2025-26 KX250 PowerFlow filter.
feedback.observed: Changed: negligible power gain but a secure seal that stops dirt being pushed past the slide-in stock filter. Suits: KX250 owners wanting engine protection. Downsides: long install; costly. Verdict: a durability upgrade, insurance for the engine.

gaps: Small bikes are thin: no written aftermarket tests found for YZ65, YZ85, KX65, KX112 or RM-Z-class minis in the sources read; only Kite Elite KX85 wheels (Dirt Bike) and Lectron CRF150R carb (MXA).

No written Showa or KYB A-kit, Ohlins or WP-conversion tests for Japanese bikes beyond the WP Pro Components KX450 test (Keefer); Keefer says he struggled to find plushness with Showa A-kits but gives no specific test.

No Honda HRC tuning-tool or Kawasaki coupler product tests found; Suzuki coupler advice only (MXA). ECU items are mostly Keefer Power Tuner and Kawasaki maps published as images, so map values are not captured.
No 2020+ piston tests found for Japanese 450s/250Fs (the Keefer Pro Circuit KX450 piston review is already in the existing files).

Many Keefer posts after 2023 are video-only (content is an embed), e.g. Keefer Tested GET RX1 Pro ECU 2023 YZ450F, FMF 4.1 slip-on 2023 YZ450F, Top 5 mods 2023 YZ450F, YZ450F flywheel weights tested (2025-11), Flo 10 mm clutch master cylinder CRF450R, Top 5 mods 2025 KX250, Kawasaki KX450 mods you can feel, Yoshimura RS-12 2027 CRF450R/YZ450F (2026-10-28); no findings were taken from them.
Many Swapmoto Mod Squad pieces are video-only; parts lists were recorded as builds without results, and no outcomes were inferred.
Dubya Edge wheels, Pro Circuit throttle tube, FLO titanium pegs, Bridgestone X31 and Ride Engineering Pulse rotor did not name a single test bike/year; bike fields say so.
